questions.question:
Which of the following sorting algorithms is the most efficient in the average case for large datasets?
a. Bubble Sort
b. Quick Sort
c. Selection Sort
d. Insertion Sort
questions.explanation: Quick Sort has average-case time complexity O(n log n) and performs best in practice for large datasets due to cache efficiency.

questions.question:
What is the time complexity of Radix Sort?
a. O(nk)
b. O(n²)
c. O(n log n)
d. O(n³)
questions.explanation: Radix Sort runs in O(nk) where n is the number of elements and k is the number of digits (passes).

questions.question:
What is the worst-case time complexity of the Quick Sort algorithm?
a. O(n log n)
b. O(n²)
c. O(n)
d. O(log n)
questions.explanation: QuickSort worst case is O(n²) — occurs when the pivot is always the smallest or largest element (e.g., sorted array with first element as pivot).

questions.question:
Which of the following is the correct time complexity for constructing a Max-Heap?
a. O(n log n)
b. O(n²)
c. O(n)
d. O(log n)
questions.explanation: Building a Max-Heap from an unsorted array takes O(n) time using the heapify-down approach starting from the last internal node.

questions.question:
Which of the following sorting algorithms has a worst-case time complexity of O(n log n)?
a) Bubble sort
b) Merge sort
c) Selection sort
d) Insertion sort
questions.explanation: Merge Sort guarantees O(n log n) in all cases — best, average and worst — making it the most consistent comparison-based sort.

questions.question:
The given array is arr = {1, 2, 4, 3}. Bubble sort is used to sort the array elements. How many iterations will be done to sort the array?
a) 4
b) 2
c) 1
d) 0
questions.explanation: Only elements 4 and 3 are out of order. Bubble sort needs 2 passes — first pass swaps 4 and 3, second pass confirms sorted order.

questions.question:
Choose the incorrect statement about merge sort from the following:
a) it is a comparison based sort
b) it is an adaptive algorithm
c) it is not an in-place algorithm
d) it is a stable algorithm

options.A: it is a comparison based sort
options.C: it is not an in-place algorithm

questions.explanation: Merge Sort is NOT adaptive — its time complexity remains O(n log n) regardless of whether the input is already sorted or not.

questions.question:
What is a randomized QuickSort?
a) The leftmost element is chosen as the pivot
b) The rightmost element is chosen as the pivot
c) Any element in the array is chosen as the pivot
d) A random number is generated which is used as the pivot

options.A: The leftmost element is chosen as the pivot
options.B: The rightmost element is chosen as the pivot
options.C: Any element in the array is chosen as the pivot
options.D: A random number is generated which is used as the pivot

questions.explanation: Randomized QuickSort selects a random element as pivot, reducing the likelihood of worst-case O(n²) behavior.

questions.question:
Which of the following algorithm implementations is similar to that of an insertion sort?
a) Binary heap
b) Quick sort
c) Merge sort
d) Radix sort
questions.explanation: Binary heap (Heap Sort) is similar to insertion sort in that it also maintains a sorted portion and inserts elements one at a time using a heap structure.

questions.question:
What is the maximum number of swaps that can be performed in the Selection Sort algorithm?
a) n-1
b) n
c) 1
d) n-2
questions.explanation: Selection Sort performs at most n-1 swaps — one swap per pass to place the minimum element in its correct position.

questions.question:
If the array is already sorted, which of these algorithms will exhibit the best performance?
a) Merge Sort
b) Insertion Sort
c) Quick Sort
d) Heap Sort
questions.explanation: Insertion Sort has O(n) best-case complexity on already-sorted arrays — it simply scans and makes no swaps.

questions.question:
What is the maximum number of swaps that can be performed in the Bubble Sort algorithm?
a) n-1
b) n
c) 1
d) n*(n-1)/2
questions.explanation: Bubble Sort in the worst case (reverse sorted array) performs n*(n-1)/2 swaps — one for every pair of adjacent elements.

questions.question:
Quick Sort algorithm is a:
a) Dynamic Programming
b) Computer programming
c) Divide & Conquer Algorithm
d) Greedy algorithm
questions.explanation: Quick Sort uses Divide & Conquer — it partitions the array around a pivot and recursively sorts subarrays.

questions.question:
Running time complexity of heap sort is ________.
a) O(n)
b) O(n²)
c) O(n log n)
d) O(log n)
questions.explanation: Heap Sort has O(n log n) time complexity in all cases — building the heap is O(n) and each of n extractions takes O(log n).

questions.question:
Time complexity of insertion sort is ________.
a) O(n)
b) O(n log n)
c) O(n²)
d) O(log n)
questions.explanation: Insertion Sort has O(n²) worst-case time complexity due to nested comparisons and shifts in a reverse-sorted array.

questions.question:
What is pivot in Quick Sort?
a) The first element of the array
b) The last element of the array
c) A reference element used to partition the array
d) The median element of the array

options.A: The first element of the array
options.B: The last element of the array
options.C: A reference element used to partition the array
options.D: The median element of the array

questions.explanation: A pivot is the reference element chosen in Quick Sort around which the array is partitioned into two subarrays.

questions.question:
Which of the following sorting algorithms is the fastest?
a) Merge sort
b) Quick sort
c) Insertion sort
d) Shell sort
questions.explanation: Quick Sort is generally the fastest in practice due to good cache performance and low constant factors despite O(n²) worst case.

questions.question:
What is the time complexity of Count Sort where n is the number of elements and k is the range of input?
a) O(n log n)
b) O(n + k)
c) O(nk)
d) O(n²)
questions.explanation: Count Sort runs in O(n + k) time — O(k) to initialize the count array and O(n) to count and reconstruct the sorted array.

questions.question:
Which of the following is true about Heap Sort?
a) It is not an in-place sorting algorithm
b) It has O(n²) worst-case time complexity
c) It is an in-place sorting algorithm with O(n log n) complexity
d) It requires O(n) extra space

options.A: It is not an in-place sorting algorithm
options.B: It has O(n²) worst-case time complexity
options.C: It is an in-place sorting algorithm with O(n log n) complexity

questions.explanation: Heap Sort is in-place (O(1) extra space) and guarantees O(n log n) time complexity in all cases.

What is the space complexity of Merge Sort?
a) O(1)
b) O(log n)
c) O(n)
d) O(n log n)
questions.explanation: Merge Sort requires O(n) auxiliary space for the temporary arrays used during the merge step.

questions.question:
What is the best-case time complexity of Bubble Sort (with optimization)?
a) O(n²)
b) O(n log n)
c) O(n)
d) O(1)
questions.explanation: With the early-exit optimization (flag for no swaps), Bubble Sort achieves O(n) best case on an already-sorted array.

Which of the following sorting algorithms is NOT stable?
a) Merge Sort
b) Insertion Sort
c) Heap Sort
d) Bubble Sort
questions.explanation: Heap Sort is NOT stable — it can change the relative order of equal elements during the heap restructuring process.
